paths.title: Software Engineer → AI Engineer
paths.subtitle: From solid coding to shipping production LLM features
paths.blurb: A guided roadmap for software engineers moving into AI engineering: sharpen interview coding, learn the ML and transformer fundamentals, then build, evaluate and operate LLM systems.

stages.title: Sharpen the fundamentals
stages.blurb: Interview-ready coding with the two patterns that solve the most problems.

stages.title: Math you'll actually use
stages.blurb: Vectors, probability and derivatives: the language of machine learning.

stages.title: Machine learning foundations
stages.blurb: How models learn, generalise and get measured.

stages.title: Deep learning and transformers
stages.blurb: From neurons to attention to large language models.

stages.title: Building with LLMs
stages.blurb: Prompts, structured output, tools, context budgets and model choice.

stages.title: RAG and retrieval
stages.blurb: Ground answers in your own data, and measure retrieval quality.

stages.title: Agents, safety and production
stages.blurb: Tool-using agents, guardrails, evals, cost and observability.

stages.title: AI system design and interviews
stages.blurb: Put it together the way interviewers will ask.

items.title: Build a small RAG assistant over docs you know, with an eval set of 100 questions. It's the best portfolio piece for this transition.

paths.title: Software Engineer → Senior Engineer
paths.subtitle: Harder problems, system design, production depth and leadership
paths.blurb: A roadmap to senior-level interviews and impact: master advanced algorithms, implement real infrastructure building blocks, design scalable systems, and lead with judgement.

stages.title: Master the core patterns
stages.blurb: Fluency with windows and pointers, including the hard variants.

stages.title: Advanced algorithms
stages.blurb: Graphs, dynamic programming and hard recursion.

stages.title: Design-coding building blocks
stages.blurb: Implement the components real systems are made of.

stages.title: System design fundamentals
stages.blurb: Scaling, data and consistency trade-offs.

stages.title: Reliability in production (Spring Boot)
stages.blurb: Resilience, rate limiting, idempotency and observability in real code.

stages.title: Front-end architecture (Angular)
stages.blurb: State, security, performance and testing on the client.

stages.title: Classic design interviews
stages.blurb: Rehearse the systems interviewers ask about most.

stages.title: Leadership and behavioural
stages.blurb: Show scope, judgement and influence.

items.title: Write down 6–8 STAR stories with numbers, then listen to them back in Listen mode the day before interviews.

paths.title: 30-Day Interview Sprint
paths.subtitle: A focused month: patterns first, mocks every week
paths.blurb: Four weeks that cover every major pattern, with a timed mock interview at the end of each week and spaced-repetition review in between.

stages.title: Week 1: windows, pointers and maps
stages.blurb: The highest-yield patterns.

stages.title: Week 2: stacks, lists and binary search
stages.blurb: Linear structures and halving.

stages.title: Week 3: trees, graphs and heaps
stages.blurb: Recursion, traversal and priority.

stages.title: Week 4: DP, backtracking and greedy
stages.blurb: The hardest category, made systematic.

items.title: Review your due cards every morning: spaced repetition keeps week 1 fresh in week 4.
